The *Kaṇikārachattiyattheraapadāna* is a verse narrative preserved within the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali canon (catalogued as Tha-Ap 167) [SuttaCentral]. Like other texts in this genre, it recounts the past karmic deeds and religious biography of an elder (*thera*). SuttaCentral records five modern translations of this text in five different languages [SuttaCentral].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus reveals substantial intra-canonical formulaic reuse, detecting 89 matching passages across 29 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The largest Pali reuse partner is the first volume of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, which shares 24 passages (2,471 characters in total, with segment §3.1–5.3 aligned with §2657–2661) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, several segments (particularly §3–7) share standardized formulaic verse material with numerous other *Therāpadāna* narratives, including the *Pañcahatthiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 47 and Tha-Ap 186), *Gaṇṭhipupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 131), and *Pupphacchattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 331) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also records cross-linguistic alignments between the opening segment (§1.1) and the Tibetan translation of the *Ārya-avalokana-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra* (D0195), though no curated external parallels are established by SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
